rows.label: Vanishing proxy with concentrated residual mass
rows.clinical_analogy: A local biomarker appears absent while residual event risk remains concentrated.
rows.reason: A vanishing proxy does not exclude concentrated residual mass.

rows.label: Positive proxy forces positive residual channel
rows.clinical_analogy: A strong warning signal correctly prevents a no-risk claim.
rows.reason: Positive proxy evidence supports warning, not reassurance.

rows.label: Vanishing proxy with added regularity structure
rows.clinical_analogy: Extra validated structure makes the proxy-to-risk implication safer.
rows.reason: Reassurance is bounded by added structure and residual-mass audit.

rows.label: Low proxy with un-audited missing-mass channel
rows.clinical_analogy: A near-zero score hides unresolved risk because no residual audit was run.
rows.reason: Residual mass remains material despite a weak proxy.

rows.label: No isolated event and low residual mass
rows.clinical_analogy: The low proxy is supported by broader context and no concentrated failure mode.
rows.reason: Reassurance is bounded by added structure and residual-mass audit.

capstone_interpretation: A vanishing local proxy cannot by itself authorize a no-risk or no-mass claim. Medical LLM monitors should require residual-risk audits before turning proxy absence into reassurance.
